newsitem.title: FINLAND: HACKMAN HAS TOO MANY BUSINESSES - CEO.
newsitem.headline: HACKMAN HAS TOO MANY BUSINESSES - CEO.

text.p: Finnish consumer goods group Oy Hackman Ab is involved in too many businesses, CEO Tapio Hintikka told a news conference on Wednesday on the publication of the group's 1996 annual report.
"Yes," Hintikka answered when asked whether Hackman was in too many different businesses.
"It is entirely possible for us to develop Hackman Designer, Metos and Hadwaco," Hintikka said listing Hackman's core businesses.
"In all other businesses, we are flexible," he said, adding that the company would keep its options open, including mergers, minority stakes or selling some operations.
Hackman's Designor unit makes tableware, cookware, household plastics and candles, and contributed 871 million markka, or 43 percent of group 1996 net sales of 1.99 billion markka.
Metos manufacturers food and beverage service equipment for industry, and generated 417 million markka, or 21 percent of group 1996 net sales.
Hadwaco, part of the group's Stainless division, produces environmental technology equipment.
The 1996 annual report did not give separate sales figures for Hadwaco, but the Hackman Stainless division had total sales of 401 million, or 20 percent of group net sales.
Hintikka said he would include the Stainless division's subcontracting operations in Hackman's core businesses, but did not elaborate.
The stainless unit also makes milk cooling and transport tanks for the dairy industry, vessels and components for the food processing industry, and tanks and equipment for the processing industry.
Hackman also produces machine knives, saw blades and machine parts for the heavy wood-processing industry through its Hackman TTT division.
Hintikka identified the group's ceramics tableware business, known especially for its Arabia brand, its plastics household wares and its dairy-related business as the main sore spots.
In 1996 Hackman fell to a 23.6 million markka loss after financial items from a 40.6 million markka profit in 1995. Net sales were down 3.3 percent to 1.99 billion markka.
Hackman expects to show a slight profit in 1997, Hintikka said, but added that he did not see satisfactory results on the group level until 1999.
"Demand is weak in our main market. Sales are expected to remain during 1997 on the same level as 1996," the group said in its annual report, repeating an earlier sales outlook.

Low capacity utilisation rates in its Designor division, dropping to around 50-60 percent last year, have hurt Hackman, and the company now plans to start selling surplus manufacturing capcity to outsiders, Hintikka said.
Hintikka said Metos, TTT, the processing industry side of the Stainless division and the frying, cookware and cutlery portion of its Designor division would be profitable this year.

"I will be satisfied if we achieve a plus-minus zero result on the dairy side this year," he said, adding that the dairy-related business accounted for about 70 percent of the Stainless unit's net sales.
Hackman's dairy-related operations are mainly concentrated in its Wedholms AB unit in Sweden and its Prominox S.A. unit in France.
Hackman, Hintikka said is increasingly working to establish itself in Europe outside its Nordic "home market" by forming partnerships abroad.
Hadwaco would soon announce a partnership agreement for global cooperation, he said
"We have had serious negotiations... I believe it will be made public in the next several weeks," Hintikka said.
--John Acher, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 235
